Settings

In HTML, scripts without a type are checked together as one Script, because they share globals. Each type="module" script is checked as a Module. Scripts with a src, and types such as application/ld+json, are skipped.
Which one do I pick?

    Not sure? Leave it on Detect from the code. HTML pages ignore this setting, because each script tag already says what it is.

    Choosing a rule set resets every rule level.
    Options for criathar/no-magic-numbers, which names each magic number. Leave empty for the defaults. Example: {"minOccurrences": 2, "style": "camelCase", "prefix": "app", "names": {"1000": "MS_PER_SECOND"}}. It also accepts the core options: ignore, ignoreArrayIndexes, ignoreDefaultValues, ignoreClassFieldInitialValues, enforceConst and detectObjects, plus ignoreConstTables (on by default).

    About Criathar

    Criathar runs ESLint on a page you can open anywhere. A parser reads your code and turns it into a tree that ESLint can check. Here the parser is acorn, not the one that comes with ESLint.

    When fixes change an inline script or style in an HTML page, the matching hashes in a Content-Security-Policy meta tag are recalculated, so the page keeps working.

    Your code stays on your device. The page only loads acorn and ESLint from a public script host.
